Got a problem with this one. In recent PR (https://github.com/JuDFTteam/best-of-atomistic-machine-learning/pull/580), sn added `description` field to project SALTED as CI/CD action update-best-of-list log said "[INFO] A project description is required with atleast 10 chars. The project SALTED will be hidden.". This is strange cause SALTED (https://github.com/andreagrisafi/SALTED) got an "About" section and this is what the Action usually pulls and puts as description. As per config guideline (projects.yaml header), description should only be added if either project is GitHub but lacks "About" section, or "About" section is not properly formatted for a suitable description, or otherwise if project is not hosted on GitHub. But I trusted the external person's judgment and merged PR. Then ran the Action to check whether this resolved it. It didn't. Instead in the new run's log (https://github.com/JuDFTteam/best-of-atomistic-machine-learning/actions/runs/31312237986/job/93241687453) I found this:

Furthermore, in the project's generator config documentation (https://github.com/best-of-lists/best-of-generator#project-quality-score), I found this about the field `homepage`: "Homepage URL of the project. Only use this property if the project homepage is different from the GitHub URL." This is also how I remembered it: A project entry does not require the field `homepage`. It is usually rendered by the update-best-of-list Action into the README.md from projects.yaml anyway. So I'm a bit surprised by this log excerpt above. Btw if you need access to the list config's defining mother projects (https://github.com/best-of-lists/best-of-generator, https://github.com/best-of-lists/best-of-update-action), I can pull them and add them to this project via add-dir command, I guess. 

So I guess there are two possible solutions for this. Either manually add `homepage` field to all the projects in projects.yaml for which the action log above complained that homepage is missing, by duplicating the resp. repo field entry (`github_id` or `gitlab_id`) as `homepage` field value. But that only fights the symptom. The other option would be to actually find the root cause of this behavior and fix it. Ideally as another PR. But that is down the line.

```text
update-best-of-list.yml
# Based on https://github.com/best-of-lists/best-of-update-action/blob/v0.8.5/workflows/update-best-of-list.yml
name: update-best-of-list

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: "Version to use for this update"
        required: false
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 18 * * 4" # Every thursday at 6pm

env:
  BRANCH_PREFIX: "update/"
  DEFAULT_BRANCH: "main"

jobs:
  update-best-of-list:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: env-update-best-of-list
    steps:
      - if: ${{ github.event.inputs != null  &&  github.event.inputs.version != null }}
        name: set-version-from-input
        run: echo "VERSION=${{ github.event.inputs.version }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
      - if: ${{ ! (env.VERSION != null && env.VERSION != '') }}
        name: set-version-via-date
        run: echo "VERSION=$(date '+%Y.%m.%d')" >> $GITHUB_ENV
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: close-stale-update-prs
        shell: bash
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          # Older auto-update PRs are always superseded by this run (README.md /
          # latest-changes.md are fully regenerated), so close them to prevent the
          # pile-up that causes merge conflicts when merged out of order.
          gh pr list --state open --json number,headRefName \
            --jq '.[] | select(.headRefName | startswith("${{ env.BRANCH_PREFIX }}")) | .number' \
          | while read -r pr; do
              gh pr close "$pr" --delete-branch --comment "Superseded by a newer best-of update." || true
            done
      - name: check-version-tag
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git fetch --tags --force
          git show-ref --tags --verify --quiet -- "refs/tags/${{ env.VERSION }}" && echo "VERSION=$(date '+%Y.%m.%d-%H.%M')" >> $GITHUB_ENV || exit 0
      - name: create-update-branch
        uses: peterjgrainger/action-create-branch@v3.0.0
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        with:
          branch: "${{ env.BRANCH_PREFIX }}${{ env.VERSION }}"
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ env.BRANCH_PREFIX }}${{ env.VERSION }}
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - name: update-best-of-list
        # original action, last update, release v0.8.5 on Jan 11, 2022
        uses: best-of-lists/best-of-update-action@v0.8.5

        # # personal fork, last update, release v0.1.1 on Aug 13, 2024
        # # for now, for debugging only
        # uses: Irratzo/best-of-lists_best-of-update-action@v0.1.1
        with:
          libraries_key: ${{ secrets.LIBRARIES_KEY }}
          github_key: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - name: push-update
        uses: stefanzweifel/git-auto-commit-action@v4
        with:
          branch: ${{ env.BRANCH_PREFIX }}${{ env.VERSION  }}
          commit_user_name: best-of update
          commit_user_email: actions@github.com
          commit_message: Update best-of list for version ${{ env.VERSION  }}
          tagging_message: ${{ env.VERSION  }}
          skip_dirty_check: true
          commit_options: "--allow-empty"
      - name: create-pull-request
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # Stops script execution if a command has an error
          set -e
          gh pr create --base ${{ env.DEFAULT_BRANCH }} --head ${{ env.BRANCH_PREFIX }}${{ env.VERSION  }} --title "Best-of update: ${{ env.VERSION  }}" --body "To finish this update: Select <code>Merge pull request</code> below and <code>Confirm merge</code>. Also, make sure to publish the created draft release in the [releases section](../releases) as well." || true
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - name: create-release
        uses: actions/create-release@v1
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        with:
          tag_name: ${{ env.VERSION  }}
          release_name: "Update: ${{ env.VERSION  }}"
          body_path: "latest-changes.md"
          draft: true
          prerelease: false
```

    for project in projects:
        project = Dict(project)

        if not project.name:
            log.info("A project name is required. Ignoring project.")
            continue

        if not project.homepage:
            log.info(

            )

        if project.group_id and not project.group:
            # Project is a grouped project -> should not be shown
            if not categories[project.category].grouped_projects:
                categories[project.category].grouped_projects = []
            categories[project.category].grouped_projects.append(project)
        elif project.show:
            if not categories[project.category].projects:
                categories[project.category].projects = []
            categories[project.category].projects.append(project)
        else:
            if not categories[project.category].hidden_projects:
                categories[project.category].hidden_projects = []
            categories[project.category].hidden_projects.append(project)

def apply_filters(project_info: Dict, configuration: Dict) -> None:
    project_info.show = True

    # Project should have atleast name, homepage, and an description longer than a few chars
    if not project_info.name:
        log.info("Could not find a valid name" + str(project_info))
        project_info.show = False
        return

    if not project_info.homepage:
        log.info(f"Could not find a valid homepage for {project_info.name}")
        project_info.show = False

    if project_info.resource:
        # Always show resources
        project_info.show = True
        return

    desc_length = 0 if not project_info.description else len(project_info.description)
    if desc_length < int(configuration.min_description_length):
        log.info(
            f"A project description is required with atleast {int(configuration.min_description_length)} chars. The project {project_info.name} will be hidden."
        )
        project_info.show = False

    # Do not show if project projectrank less than min_projectrank
    if (
        configuration.min_projectrank
        and project_info.projectrank
        and int(project_info.projectrank) < int(configuration.min_projectrank)
    ):
        project_info.show = False

    # Do not show if project stars less than min_stars
    if (
        configuration.min_stars
        and project_info.star_count
        and int(project_info.star_count) < int(configuration.min_stars)
    ):
        project_info.show = False

    # Check platform requires
    if configuration.require_repo and not (
        project_info.github_url or project_info.gitlab_url
    ):
        log.info(
            f"{project_info.name} requires a repo url (e.g. GitHub or GitLab), but no repo url found."

```text
import logging
import os
import re
import time
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Optional

import requests
from addict import Dict
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from dateutil.parser import parse

from best_of import default_config, utils
from best_of.default_config import MIN_PROJECT_DESC_LENGTH
from best_of.integrations import libio_integration

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def get_repo_deps_via_github(github_id: str) -> int:
    try:
        request = requests.get(
            "https://github.com/" + github_id + "/network/dependents"
        )
        if request.status_code != 200:
            log.info(
                "Unable to find repo dependents via GitHub api: "
                + github_id
                + " ("
                + str(request.status_code)
                + ")"
            )
            return 0
        repo_deps = 0
        soup = BeautifulSoup(request.text, "html.parser")
        repo_deps_str = soup.find(string=re.compile(r"[0-9,]+\s+Repositories"))
        if repo_deps_str:
            count_search = re.search("([0-9,]+)", repo_deps_str, re.IGNORECASE)
            if count_search:
                repo_deps += int(count_search.group(1).replace(",", ""))
        pkg_deps_str = soup.find(string=re.compile(r"[0-9,]+\s+Packages"))
        if pkg_deps_str:
            count_search = re.search("([0-9,]+)", pkg_deps_str, re.IGNORECASE)
            if count_search:
                repo_deps += int(count_search.group(1).replace(",", ""))
        return repo_deps
    except Exception as ex:
        log.info(
            "Unable to find repo dependents via GitHub api: " + github_id, exc_info=ex
        )
        return 0


def get_contributors_via_github_api(
    github_id: str, github_api_token: str
) -> Optional[int]:
    if not github_id or not github_api_token:
        return None

    try:
        request = requests.get(
            "https://api.github.com/repos/"
            + github_id
            + "/contributors?page=1&per_page=1&anon=True",
            headers={"Authorization": "token " + github_api_token},
        )
        if request.status_code != 200:
            log.info(
                "Unable to find repo contributors via GitHub api: "
                + github_id
                + " ("
                + str(request.status_code)
                + ")"
            )
            return None

        if "Link" not in request.headers or not request.headers["Link"]:
            return None

        link_header = request.headers["Link"]

        contributor_count = 0
        for found_group in re.findall(r"\?page=([0-9]+)", link_header, re.IGNORECASE):
            contributor_count = max(contributor_count, int(found_group))
        return contributor_count
    except Exception as ex:
        log.info(
            "Unable to find repo dependents via GitHub api: " + github_id,
            exc_info=ex,
        )

        return None


def request_metadata_from_github_api(
    github_api_token: str, github_id: str, recent_activity_date: datetime
) -> Optional[Dict]:

    owner = github_id.split("/")[0]
    repo = github_id.split("/")[1]

    # TODO: parse github dependents: https://github.com/badgen/badgen.net/blob/master/endpoints/github.ts#L406
    # TODO: Github assets download: https://github.com/badgen/badgen.net/blob/master/endpoints/github.ts#L125
    # TODO: latest stable release, PR...
    # discussions {
    #   totalCount
    # }
    # isArchived
    # isDisabled
    # isEmpty
    # isFork
    # isInOrganization
    # isSecurityPolicyEnabled
    # hasIssuesEnabled

    # GraphQL query
    # https://github.com/badgen/badgen.net/blob/master/endpoints/github.ts#L214
    query = """
query($owner: String!, $repo: String!, $since_recent_activity: GitTimestamp!) {
  repository(owner: $owner, name: $repo) {
    name
    nameWithOwner
    description
    url
    homepageUrl
    createdAt
    updatedAt
    pushedAt
    diskUsage
    primaryLanguage {
      name
    }
    licenseInfo {
      spdxId
    }
    stargazers {
      totalCount
    }
    pullRequests {
      totalCount
    }
    forks {
      totalCount
    }
    watchers {
      totalCount
    }
    masterCommit: defaultBranchRef {
        target {
          ... on Commit {
            committedDate
            recent_activity: history(since: $since_recent_activity) {
                totalCount
            }
            history {
                totalCount
            }
          }
        }
    }
    repositoryTopics(first: 100) {
      nodes {
        topic {
          name
        }
      }
    }
    openIssues: issues(states: OPEN) {
      totalCount
    }
    closedIssues: issues(states: CLOSED) {
      totalCount
    }
    releases(first: 100, orderBy: {field:CREATED_AT, direction:DESC}) {
      nodes {
        createdAt
        publishedAt
        tagName
        isDraft
        isPrerelease
        releaseAssets(first: 100) {
          nodes {
            downloadCount
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
"""
    headers = {"Authorization": "token " + github_api_token}
    variables = {
        "owner": owner,
        "repo": repo,
        "since_recent_activity": recent_activity_date.isoformat(),
    }

    try:
        response = requests.post(
            "https://api.github.com/graphql",
            json={"query": query, "variables": variables},
            headers=headers,
        )

        if response.status_code != 200:
            log.info(
                "Unable to find GitHub repo via GitHub api: "
                + github_id
                + " ("
                + str(response.status_code)
                + ")"
            )
            return None
        response_data = response.json()

        if "data" not in response_data:
            log.info("Request returned unexpected data: ", response_data)
            return None

        return Dict(response_data["data"]["repository"])
    except Exception as ex:
        log.info(
            "Failed to request GitHub repo via GitHub api: " + github_id,
            exc_info=ex,
        )
        return None


def update_via_github_api(project_info: Dict) -> None:
    if not project_info.github_id:
        return

    if "/" not in project_info.github_id:
        log.info("The GitHub project id is not valid: " + project_info.github_id)
        return

    github_api_token = os.getenv("GITHUB_API_KEY")
    if not github_api_token:
        return None

    # Check activity since the latest 90 days
    recent_activity_date = datetime.now() - timedelta(
        days=default_config.RECENT_ACTIVITY_DAYS
    )

    github_info = request_metadata_from_github_api(
        github_api_token, project_info.github_id, recent_activity_date
    )
    if github_info is None:
        log.info("Retrying failed github api call short wait time.")
        time.sleep(150)
        github_info = request_metadata_from_github_api(
            github_api_token, project_info.github_id, recent_activity_date
        )

    if github_info is None:
        return

    if not project_info.github_url and github_info.url:
        project_info.github_url = github_info.url

    if not project_info.homepage:
        project_info.homepage = project_info.github_url

    if not project_info.name and github_info.name:
        project_info.name = github_info.name

    if github_info.nameWithOwner and utils.simplify_str(
        project_info.github_id
    ) != utils.simplify_str(github_info.nameWithOwner):
        log.info(
            f"The GitHub repo name has changed from {project_info.github_id} to {github_info.nameWithOwner}"
        )
        project_info.updated_github_id = github_info.nameWithOwner

    if (
        not project_info.license
        and github_info.licenseInfo
        and github_info.licenseInfo.spdxId
    ):
        # if licenses is noassertion, then it is not provided
        if github_info.licenseInfo.spdxId.lower() != "noassertion":
            project_info.license = github_info.licenseInfo.spdxId

    if github_info.createdAt:
        try:
            created_at = parse(str(github_info.createdAt), ignoretz=True)
            if not project_info.created_at:
                project_info.created_at = created_at
            elif project_info.created_at > created_at:
                # always use the oldest available date
                project_info.created_at = created_at
        except Exception as ex:
            log.warning(
                "Failed to parse timestamp: " + str(github_info.createdAt), exc_info=ex
            )

    # pushed_at is the last github push, updated_at is the last sync?
    if github_info.pushedAt:
        try:
            updated_at = parse(str(github_info.pushedAt), ignoretz=True)
            if not project_info.updated_at:
                project_info.updated_at = updated_at
            elif project_info.updated_at < updated_at:
                # always use the latest available date
                project_info.updated_at = updated_at
        except Exception as ex:
            log.warning(
                "Failed to parse timestamp: " + str(github_info.pushedAt), exc_info=ex
            )

    if github_info.masterCommit and github_info.masterCommit.target:
        if github_info.masterCommit.target.committedDate:
            try:
                last_commit_pushed_at = parse(
                    str(github_info.masterCommit.target.committedDate), ignoretz=True
                )
                if not project_info.last_commit_pushed_at:
                    project_info.last_commit_pushed_at = last_commit_pushed_at
                elif project_info.last_commit_pushed_at < last_commit_pushed_at:
                    # always use the latest available date
                    project_info.last_commit_pushed_at = last_commit_pushed_at
            except Exception as ex:
                log.warning(
                    "Failed to parse timestamp: "
                    + str(github_info.target.committedDate),
                    exc_info=ex,
                )
        if (
            github_info.masterCommit.target.history
            and github_info.masterCommit.target.history.totalCount
        ):
            project_info.commit_count = int(
                github_info.masterCommit.target.history.totalCount
            )

        if (
            github_info.masterCommit.target.recent_activity
            and github_info.masterCommit.target.recent_activity.totalCount
        ):
            # TODO: combine pullrequests, closed issues and commit count into one recent acitivty score
            project_info.recent_commit_count = int(
                github_info.masterCommit.target.recent_activity.totalCount
            )

    if github_info.forks and github_info.forks.totalCount:
        fork_count = int(github_info.forks.totalCount)
        if not project_info.fork_count:
            project_info.fork_count = fork_count
        elif int(project_info.fork_count) < fork_count:
            # always use the highest number
            project_info.fork_count = fork_count

    if github_info.watchers and github_info.watchers.totalCount:
        watchers_count = int(github_info.watchers.totalCount)
        if not project_info.watchers_count:
            project_info.watchers_count = watchers_count
        elif int(project_info.watchers_count) < watchers_count:
            # always use the highest number
            project_info.watchers_count = watchers_count

    if github_info.pullRequests and github_info.pullRequests.totalCount:
        pr_count = int(github_info.pullRequests.totalCount)
        if not project_info.pr_count:
            project_info.pr_count = pr_count
        elif int(project_info.pr_count) < pr_count:
            # always use the highest number
            project_info.pr_count = pr_count

    if github_info.openIssues and github_info.openIssues.totalCount:
        open_issue_count = int(github_info.openIssues.totalCount)
        if not project_info.open_issue_count:
            project_info.open_issue_count = open_issue_count
        elif int(project_info.open_issue_count) < open_issue_count:
            # always use the highest number
            project_info.open_issue_count = open_issue_count

def update_via_github(project_info: Dict) -> None:
    if not project_info.github_id:
        return

    update_via_github_api(project_info)

    if not project_info.github_url or (
        project_info.star_count and project_info.star_count > 20
    ):
        # small projects cannot be found on liberies.io often
        libio_integration.update_repo_via_libio(project_info)


def generate_github_details(project: Dict, configuration: Dict) -> str:
    github_id = project.github_id
    if not github_id:
        return ""

    metrics_md = ""
    if project.contributor_count:
        if metrics_md:
            metrics_md += " · "
        metrics_md += "👨‍💻 " + str(utils.simplify_number(project.contributor_count))

    if project.fork_count:
        if metrics_md:
            metrics_md += " · "
        metrics_md += "🔀 " + str(utils.simplify_number(project.fork_count))

    if project.github_release_downloads:
        if metrics_md:
            metrics_md += " · "
        metrics_md += "📥 " + str(
            utils.simplify_number(project.github_release_downloads)
        )

    if project.github_dependent_project_count:
        if metrics_md:
            metrics_md += " · "
        metrics_md += "📦 " + str(
            utils.simplify_number(project.github_dependent_project_count)
        )

    if project.open_issue_count and project.closed_issue_count:
        if metrics_md:
            metrics_md += " · "
        total_issues = project.closed_issue_count + project.open_issue_count

        metrics_md += (
            "📋 "
            + str(utils.simplify_number(total_issues))
            + " - "
            + str(
                int(
                    (
                        project.open_issue_count
                        / (project.closed_issue_count + project.open_issue_count)
                    )
                    * 100
                )
            )
            + "% open"
        )

    if project.last_commit_pushed_at:
        if metrics_md:
            metrics_md += " · "
        metrics_md += "⏱️ " + str(project.last_commit_pushed_at.strftime("%d.%m.%Y"))

    if metrics_md:
        metrics_md = " (" + metrics_md + ")"

    github_url = ""
    if project.github_url:
        github_url = project.github_url

    # https://badgen.net/#github

    # only show : if details are available
    seperator = (
        ""
        if not configuration.generate_badges
        and not configuration.generate_install_hints
        else ":"
    )

    details_md = "- [GitHub](" + github_url + ")" + metrics_md + seperator + "\n"

    if configuration.generate_install_hints:
        details_md += "\n\t```\n\tgit clone https://github.com/{github_id}\n\t```\n"
    return details_md.format(github_id=github_id)

```text
#!/bin/bash

# Stops script execution if a command has an error
set -e

# set default generation args if not provided
GENERATE_ARGS="$INPUT_GENERATE_ARGS"
if [ -z "$GENERATE_ARGS" ]; then
    # currently no default args
    GENERATE_ARGS=""
fi

if [ -n "$INPUT_LIBRARIES_KEY" ]; then
    GENERATE_ARGS="$GENERATE_ARGS --libraries-key=$INPUT_LIBRARIES_KEY"
fi

if [ -z "$INPUT_PROJECTS_FILE" ]; then
    # set default
    INPUT_PROJECTS_FILE="projects.yaml"
fi

if [ -n "$INPUT_GITHUB_KEY" ]; then
    # Use github token from inputs
    GENERATE_ARGS="$GENERATE_ARGS --github-key=$INPUT_GITHUB_KEY"
elif [ -n "$GITHUB_TOKEN" ]; then
    # Use github token provided via Github Actions
    GENERATE_ARGS="$GENERATE_ARGS --github-key=$GITHUB_TOKEN"
fi

# Navigate to the github action home directory
if [ -n "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ]; then
    cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
fi

# Print commands
set -x

# Execute generation script
best-of generate $GENERATE_ARGS $INPUT_PROJECTS_FILE

**The GitHub GraphQL call has been failing for every project since the 2026-07-23 run.** Comparing history CSVs (fields that *only* come from the generator's GraphQL query):

| field | 07-19 | 07-23 → 08-09 |
|---|---|---|
| `commit_count` | 456 | **1** |

| `github_url` | 457 | 390 |
| `contributor_count` (REST, not GraphQL) | 415 | **436** ✓ |

The 1 + 7 survivors are GitLab-hosted projects. REST still works (contributor counts went *up*), so the token is valid — GraphQL specifically is denied. MACE shows the damage: `📋 620 - 23% open · ⏱️ 15.07.2026` → gone, rank 🥇23 → 🥈14.

No GraphQL → no description (hence the first log line) *and* no `homepage` → `categorize_projects` drops it entirely. 174 shown + 291 hidden + 52 dropped = 517. The 52 are exactly the projects with no package-manager ID, so libraries.io couldn't rescue them either.

The `description` added in PR #580 was treating a symptom of a list-wide outage.

```md
# Fix: GitHub GraphQL metadata fetch is silently failing in `update-best-of-list`

## Context

Since the **2026-07-23** Action run, the `best-of` generator has been unable to fetch *any*
GitHub repository metadata via the GraphQL API. The failure is silent — nothing is logged at
warning/error level, the job stays green, and a PR is opened as usual. Three weeks of best-of
update PRs have been merged on top of degraded data.

SALTED was only the visible tip: PR #580 added a manual `description` to work around the
`"A project description is required"` log line, but that description was missing because the
GitHub "About" text is fetched through the same broken GraphQL call.

### Evidence

Fields in `history/*_projects.csv` that are populated **only** by the generator's GraphQL query
collapse between the 07-19 and 07-23 runs, while the REST-based field keeps working:

| field | source | 07-19 | 07-23 → 08-09 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `commit_count` | GraphQL | 456 | **1** |
| `closed_issue_count` | GraphQL | 340 | **7** |
| `github_url` | GraphQL, libraries.io fallback | 457 | 390 |
| `star_count` | GraphQL, libraries.io fallback | 468 | 407 |
| `contributor_count` | GitHub **REST** | 415 | **436** ✓ |
| `show == True` | derived | 242 | **174** |

The 1 `commit_count` and 7 `closed_issue_count` survivors are all GitLab-hosted projects
(empty `github_id`) — i.e. **zero** GitHub GraphQL queries succeeded. `contributor_count` comes
from a plain REST call (`/repos/{id}/contributors`) with the *same* token and actually improved,
so the token is valid and the network path is fine. The breakage is specific to GraphQL.

User-visible damage, e.g. MACE:

\```
07-19: (🥇23 · ⭐ 1.3K) … - [GitHub](…) (👨‍💻 72 · 🔀 430 · 📋 620 - 23% open · ⏱️ 15.07.2026):
08-09: (🥈14 · ⭐ 1.2K) … - [GitHub](…) (👨‍💻 77 · 🔀 420):
\```

Issue counts and last-commit dates are gone list-wide, stars are stale (libraries.io values),
and project ranks have dropped across the board.

### Why 52 projects disappear entirely

`categorize_projects` in `best_of/projects_collection.py` skips any project without a `homepage`:

\```python
if not project.homepage:
    log.info("A project homepage is required. Ignoring project: " + project.name)
    continue
\```

`homepage` is normally filled from `github_info.url` inside `update_via_github_api`. With GraphQL
dead, the only remaining source is the libraries.io fallback — which knows nothing about repos
that have no published package. The 52 complained-about projects are **exactly** the entries in
`projects.yaml` with a `github_id` and no package-manager id (`pypi_id`, `conda_id`, …) and no
manual `homepage`. Accounting checks out: 174 shown + 291 hidden + 52 dropped = 517.

### Root cause hypothesis (to be confirmed in step 1)

`request_metadata_from_github_api` (best-of 0.8.5) ends with:

\```python
if response.status_code != 200: … return None      # -> caller sleeps 150 s and retries
return Dict(response_data["data"]["repository"])   # addict: Dict(None) == {}  -> falsy, no retry
\```

The 08-09 run processed 523 projects in 19:52 (≈2.3 s/project), so the 150-second retry path was
**never** taken. That rules out HTTP 401/403 and GraphQL `RATE_LIMITED` (which returns
`"data": null` and would raise → `None` → retry). The only shape consistent with the timing is
**HTTP 200 with `data.repository = null`** plus an `errors` array — i.e. `FORBIDDEN`
("Resource not accessible by integration") or `NOT_FOUND`.

That is the signature of the Actions-provided `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` no longer being able to
resolve *other* repositories through GraphQL. The workflow passes it as `github_key`:

\```yaml
uses: best-of-lists/best-of-update-action@v0.8.5
with:
  github_key: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
\```

Nothing changed in this repo between the good 07-19 run and the broken 07-23 run
(`git log --since=2026-07-15 --until=2026-07-26` shows only the update commits), so the change
came from GitHub's side. Running the generator's exact GraphQL query locally with a personal
access token succeeds for all sampled repos (SALTED, cnine, LapNet, mace) — confirming the query
itself is still valid and the problem is the token.

**Not confirmed yet:** the literal error string GitHub returns. Step 1 settles it.

## Plan

Single PR, branch e.g. `fix/github-graphql-token`.

### 1. Confirm the failure mode (temporary debug step)

Add a step to [.github/workflows/update-best-of-list.yml](.github/workflows/update-best-of-list.yml)
immediately before the `update-best-of-list` step, run it once via `workflow_dispatch`, read the
output, then delete it before merging:

\```yaml
      - name: debug-graphql-token
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          curl -sS -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' \
            -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
            -d '{"query":"{repository(owner:\"andreagrisafi\",name:\"SALTED\"){url stargazers{totalCount}}}"}' \
            https://api.github.com/graphql
\```

Expected if the hypothesis holds: `HTTP 200` with `"repository": null` and an `errors` entry of
type `FORBIDDEN` or `NOT_FOUND`. If instead it returns real data, the hypothesis is wrong and the
investigation moves to the retry/timing path — do not proceed to step 2 in that case.

### 2. Use a PAT for the generator's GitHub key

1. Create a **classic** personal access token with **no scopes selected** (this already grants
   public-repository read, which is all the generator needs). Fine-grained tokens work too:
   "Public Repositories (read-only)".
2. Store it as secret `GH_API_TOKEN` in the **`env-update-best-of-list` environment** (the job
   declares `environment: env-update-best-of-list`, same place as `LIBRARIES_KEY`).
3. In [.github/workflows/update-best-of-list.yml](.github/workflows/update-best-of-list.yml),
   change only the generator step:

\```yaml
        with:
          libraries_key: ${{ secrets.LIBRARIES_KEY }}
          github_key: ${{ secrets.GH_API_TOKEN }}
\```

Leave every other `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` use (checkout, `git-auto-commit-action`, `gh pr create`,
`create-release`) untouched — those act on this repo and are unaffected.

### 3. Add a canary so the next silent break is loud

The whole point of this incident is that a total metadata outage produced a green run. Add one
step **after** `update-best-of-list` and **before** `push-update`, so a broken generation never
becomes a PR:

\```yaml
      - name: check-generation-sanity
        shell: bash
        run: |
          python3 - <<'EOF'
          import csv, glob, sys
          # ponytail: absolute fill-rate floor, not a diff vs the previous run — catches a total
          # GraphQL outage, which is the failure that actually happened. Tighten if it ever flaps.
          f = sorted(glob.glob("history/*_projects.csv"))[-1]
          rows = [r for r in csv.DictReader(open(f)) if r["github_id"]]
          filled = sum(1 for r in rows if r["commit_count"])
          print(f"{f}: {filled}/{len(rows)} GitHub projects have commit_count")
          if filled < 0.5 * len(rows):
              sys.exit("GitHub GraphQL metadata fetch looks broken - refusing to publish.")
          EOF
\```

`commit_count` is the cleanest sentinel: it is populated *only* by the GraphQL query and has no
libraries.io fallback, so it goes to ~0 the moment GraphQL breaks and stays high otherwise
(456/459 on 07-19).

### 4. Revert the SALTED workaround

In [projects.yaml](projects.yaml#L1716-L1719), drop the `description:` line added by PR #580 —
SALTED has a proper GitHub "About" section, so per the `projects.yaml` header guideline the
description must come from there:

\```yaml
- name: SALTED
  category: ml-dft

## Approved Plan:
# Fix: GitHub GraphQL metadata fetch is silently failing in `update-best-of-list`

## Context

Since the **2026-07-23** Action run, the `best-of` generator has been unable to fetch *any*
GitHub repository metadata via the GraphQL API. The failure is silent — nothing is logged at
warning/error level, the job stays green, and a PR is opened as usual. Three weeks of best-of
update PRs have been merged on top of degraded data.

SALTED was only the visible tip: PR #580 added a manual `description` to work around the
`"A project description is required"` log line, but that description was missing because the
GitHub "About" text is fetched through the same broken GraphQL call.

### Evidence

Fields in `history/*_projects.csv` that are populated **only** by the generator's GraphQL query
collapse between the 07-19 and 07-23 runs, while the REST-based field keeps working:

| field | source | 07-19 | 07-23 → 08-09 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `commit_count` | GraphQL | 456 | **1** |
| `closed_issue_count` | GraphQL | 340 | **7** |
| `github_url` | GraphQL, libraries.io fallback | 457 | 390 |
| `star_count` | GraphQL, libraries.io fallback | 468 | 407 |
| `contributor_count` | GitHub **REST** | 415 | **436** ✓ |
| `show == True` | derived | 242 | **174** |

The 1 `commit_count` and 7 `closed_issue_count` survivors are all GitLab-hosted projects
(empty `github_id`) — i.e. **zero** GitHub GraphQL queries succeeded. `contributor_count` comes
from a plain REST call (`/repos/{id}/contributors`) with the *same* token and actually improved,
so the token is valid and the network path is fine. The breakage is specific to GraphQL.

User-visible damage, e.g. MACE:

```
07-19: (🥇23 · ⭐ 1.3K) … - [GitHub](…) (👨‍💻 72 · 🔀 430 · 📋 620 - 23% open · ⏱️ 15.07.2026):
08-09: (🥈14 · ⭐ 1.2K) … - [GitHub](…) (👨‍💻 77 · 🔀 420):
```

Issue counts and last-commit dates are gone list-wide, stars are stale (libraries.io values),
and project ranks have dropped across the board.

### Why 52 projects disappear entirely

`categorize_projects` in `best_of/projects_collection.py` skips any project without a `homepage`:

```python
if not project.homepage:
    log.info("A project homepage is required. Ignoring project: " + project.name)
    continue
```

`homepage` is normally filled from `github_info.url` inside `update_via_github_api`. With GraphQL
dead, the only remaining source is the libraries.io fallback — which knows nothing about repos
that have no published package. The 52 complained-about projects are **exactly** the entries in
`projects.yaml` with a `github_id` and no package-manager id (`pypi_id`, `conda_id`, …) and no
manual `homepage`. Accounting checks out: 174 shown + 291 hidden + 52 dropped = 517.

### Root cause hypothesis (to be confirmed in step 1)

`request_metadata_from_github_api` (best-of 0.8.5) ends with:

```python
if response.status_code != 200: … return None      # -> caller sleeps 150 s and retries
return Dict(response_data["data"]["repository"])   # addict: Dict(None) == {}  -> falsy, no retry
```

The 08-09 run processed 523 projects in 19:52 (≈2.3 s/project), so the 150-second retry path was
**never** taken. That rules out HTTP 401/403 and GraphQL `RATE_LIMITED` (which returns
`"data": null` and would raise → `None` → retry). The only shape consistent with the timing is
**HTTP 200 with `data.repository = null`** plus an `errors` array — i.e. `FORBIDDEN`
("Resource not accessible by integration") or `NOT_FOUND`.

That is the signature of the Actions-provided `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` no longer being able to
resolve *other* repositories through GraphQL. The workflow passes it as `github_key`:

```yaml
uses: best-of-lists/best-of-update-action@v0.8.5
with:
  github_key: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

Nothing changed in this repo between the good 07-19 run and the broken 07-23 run
(`git log --since=2026-07-15 --until=2026-07-26` shows only the update commits), so the change
came from GitHub's side. Running the generator's exact GraphQL query locally with a personal
access token succeeds for all sampled repos (SALTED, cnine, LapNet, mace) — confirming the query
itself is still valid and the problem is the token.

**Not confirmed yet:** the literal error string GitHub returns. Step 1 settles it.

## Plan

Single PR, branch e.g. `fix/github-graphql-token`.

### 1. Confirm the failure mode (temporary debug step)

Add a step to [.github/workflows/update-best-of-list.yml](.github/workflows/update-best-of-list.yml)
immediately before the `update-best-of-list` step, run it once via `workflow_dispatch`, read the
output, then delete it before merging:

```yaml
      - name: debug-graphql-token
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          curl -sS -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' \
            -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
            -d '{"query":"{repository(owner:\"andreagrisafi\",name:\"SALTED\"){url stargazers{totalCount}}}"}' \
            https://api.github.com/graphql
```

Expected if the hypothesis holds: `HTTP 200` with `"repository": null` and an `errors` entry of
type `FORBIDDEN` or `NOT_FOUND`. If instead it returns real data, the hypothesis is wrong and the
investigation moves to the retry/timing path — do not proceed to step 2 in that case.

### 2. Use a PAT for the generator's GitHub key

1. Create a **classic** personal access token with **no scopes selected** (this already grants
   public-repository read, which is all the generator needs). Fine-grained tokens work too:
   "Public Repositories (read-only)".
2. Store it as secret `GH_API_TOKEN` in the **`env-update-best-of-list` environment** (the job
   declares `environment: env-update-best-of-list`, same place as `LIBRARIES_KEY`).
3. In [.github/workflows/update-best-of-list.yml](.github/workflows/update-best-of-list.yml),
   change only the generator step:

```yaml
        with:
          libraries_key: ${{ secrets.LIBRARIES_KEY }}
          github_key: ${{ secrets.GH_API_TOKEN }}
```

Leave every other `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` use (checkout, `git-auto-commit-action`, `gh pr create`,
`create-release`) untouched — those act on this repo and are unaffected.

### 3. Add a canary so the next silent break is loud

The whole point of this incident is that a total metadata outage produced a green run. Add one
step **after** `update-best-of-list` and **before** `push-update`, so a broken generation never
becomes a PR:

```yaml
      - name: check-generation-sanity
        shell: bash
        run: |
          python3 - <<'EOF'
          import csv, glob, sys
          # ponytail: absolute fill-rate floor, not a diff vs the previous run — catches a total
          # GraphQL outage, which is the failure that actually happened. Tighten if it ever flaps.
          f = sorted(glob.glob("history/*_projects.csv"))[-1]
          rows = [r for r in csv.DictReader(open(f)) if r["github_id"]]
          filled = sum(1 for r in rows if r["commit_count"])
          print(f"{f}: {filled}/{len(rows)} GitHub projects have commit_count")
          if filled < 0.5 * len(rows):
              sys.exit("GitHub GraphQL metadata fetch looks broken - refusing to publish.")
          EOF
```

`commit_count` is the cleanest sentinel: it is populated *only* by the GraphQL query and has no
libraries.io fallback, so it goes to ~0 the moment GraphQL breaks and stays high otherwise
(456/459 on 07-19).

### 4. Revert the SALTED workaround

In [projects.yaml](projects.yaml#L1716-L1719), drop the `description:` line added by PR #580 —
SALTED has a proper GitHub "About" section, so per the `projects.yaml` header guideline the
description must come from there:

```yaml
- name: SALTED
  category: ml-dft
  github_id: andreagrisafi/SALTED
```

Do this in the same PR, but verify in step 5 that SALTED reappears with the fetched description
before merging.

### Explicitly not doing

**Do not add `homepage:` to the 52 complained-about projects.** It fixes only their disappearance
while leaving all ~459 GitHub entries with missing issue counts, missing commit dates, stale star
counts and depressed ranks — and it would bake in 52 redundant fields that violate the
`projects.yaml` guideline once the real fix lands.

Verified where it needs to go: there are **no repo-level secrets** — `LIBRARIES_KEY` is an *environment* secret on `env-update-best-of-list`. `GH_API_TOKEN` goes in the same place.

## A. Create the token

1. Open **https://github.com/settings/tokens/new** (Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → **Tokens (classic)** → Generate new token (classic)).
2. **Note:** `best-of-aml metadata read` — so future-you knows what it's for.
3. **Expiration:** `No expiration`. GitHub will warn about this; it's the right call for an unattended weekly job. If your org policy forbids it, pick `1 year` and set a reminder — the new canary will fail the run loudly when it expires, but you'd rather not find out that way.
4. **Scopes: tick nothing at all.** Leave every checkbox unchecked. A zero-scope classic token can read public repository data over both REST and GraphQL, which is everything the generator needs. Do not tick `repo` — that would hand the token write access to all your private repos for no benefit.
5. Click **Generate token** and copy the `ghp_…` value. It's shown exactly once.

## B. Store it as an environment secret

Run this — `gh` prompts for the value, so the token never lands in your shell history:

```
gh secret set GH_API_TOKEN \
  --env env-update-best-of-list \
  --repo JuDFTteam/best-of-atomistic-machine-learning
```

## C. Verify

```

## Problem

Since the **2026-07-23** run, `update-best-of-list` has fetched **no GitHub repository metadata at all**. The job stayed green the whole time and kept opening update PRs, so three weeks of updates were merged on top of degraded data.

#580 was the first visible symptom: a manual `description` was added to SALTED because the Action logged `A project description is required`. But SALTED has a perfectly good "About" section — it just was not being fetched.

## Evidence

Fields in `history/*_projects.csv` that only the generator's **GraphQL** query populates collapse between the last good run and the first bad one, while the **REST**-backed field keeps working:

| field | source | 07-19 | 07-23 → 08-09 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `commit_count` | GraphQL only | 456 | **1** |
| `closed_issue_count` | GraphQL only | 340 | **7** |
| `github_url` | GraphQL, libraries.io fallback | 457 | 390 |
| `star_count` | GraphQL, libraries.io fallback | 468 | 407 |
| `contributor_count` | GitHub **REST** | 415 | **436** ✅ |
| `show == True` | derived | 242 | **174** |

The 1 `commit_count` and 7 `closed_issue_count` survivors are all GitLab-hosted projects (empty `github_id`) — i.e. **zero** GitHub GraphQL queries succeeded. `contributor_count` comes from a plain REST call using the *same* token and actually went up, so the token is valid and the network path is fine. The breakage is specific to GraphQL.

User-visible damage, e.g. MACE:

\```
07-19: (🥇23 · ⭐ 1.3K) … - [GitHub](…) (👨‍💻 72 · 🔀 430 · 📋 620 - 23% open · ⏱️ 15.07.2026):
08-09: (🥈14 · ⭐ 1.2K) … - [GitHub](…) (👨‍💻 77 · 🔀 420):
\```

Issue counts and last-commit dates gone list-wide, stars stale, ranks depressed.

### Why 52 projects vanished from the README entirely

`categorize_projects` drops any project without a `homepage`:

\```python
if not project.homepage:
    log.info("A project homepage is required. Ignoring project: " + project.name)
    continue
\```

`homepage` normally comes from `github_info.url`. With GraphQL dead the only remaining source is the libraries.io fallback, which knows nothing about repos that publish no package. The 52 projects in the log are **exactly** the `projects.yaml` entries that have a `github_id`, no package-manager id, and no manual `homepage`. The arithmetic checks out: 174 shown + 291 hidden + 52 dropped = 517.

## Root cause

The Actions-provided `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` can no longer resolve *other* repositories through the GitHub GraphQL API. Nothing changed in this repo between the good and bad runs, and the generator's exact GraphQL query still succeeds from a personal access token (verified locally against SALTED, cnine, LapNet and mace) — so the change came from GitHub's side.

**best-of 0.8.5 hides the failure.** `request_metadata_from_github_api` ends with:

\```python
if response.status_code != 200: … return None      # -> caller sleeps 150 s and retries
return Dict(response_data["data"]["repository"])   # addict: Dict(None) == {} -> falsy, but NOT None
\```

A `200` carrying `"repository": null` becomes an empty `addict.Dict`: falsy, so every downstream field is skipped, but not `None`, so nothing is logged and the retry never fires. That also matches the timing — the 08-09 run did 523 projects in 19:52 (~2.3 s each), so the 150-second retry path was never taken, which rules out 401/403 and GraphQL `RATE_LIMITED` (both of which would have gone down the retry branch). The `homepage: '{}'` values sitting in the history CSVs are that empty `Dict` serialised.

## Changes

- **`github_key` now uses `secrets.GH_API_TOKEN`** — a classic PAT with *no scopes*, which is all that public-repo reads need. Added as an environment secret on `env-update-best-of-list` next to `LIBRARIES_KEY`. Every other `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` use (checkout, commit, `gh pr create`, release) is untouched; those act on this repo and work fine.
- **`check-generation-sanity`** — new step between generation and push, so a broken generation can never become a PR. `commit_count` is the sentinel: only the GraphQL query sets it and there is no fallback, so it drops to ~0 the instant GraphQL stops answering. Self-tested against the real CSVs: 0/459 on the broken run → exit 1, 455/459 on the last good run → exit 0.
- **Reverted the SALTED `description`** from #580 — with GraphQL working the description comes from the About section again, per the `projects.yaml` header guideline. Thanks @zekunlou for surfacing the symptom.
- **`debug-graphql-token`** — temporary, prints the raw GraphQL response for both tokens side by side. **Delete before merging**, once the output is recorded below.

## Not done deliberately

Adding `homepage:` to the 52 complained-about projects. It would fix only their disappearance while leaving all ~459 GitHub entries with missing issue counts, missing commit dates, stale stars and depressed ranks — and would bake in 52 redundant fields that contradict the `projects.yaml` guideline once the real fix lands.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-08-09 15:40:16Z)**_

Done and verified end to end.

## Root cause, confirmed

The Actions `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` is denied the **`stargazers`** field on repositories it doesn't own. GitHub returns HTTP 200 with `"type":"FORBIDDEN"`; because that field is non-nullable, the null propagates up and nulls the entire `repository` object. best-of 0.8.5 converts that into an empty `addict.Dict` — falsy but not `None` — so no error is logged and the retry never fires. Total outage, zero signal.

My earlier reasoning had the mechanism right but the location slightly off: I'd assumed the denial was on the repository, not on a single field within it. Same outcome, and the field-level detail is what explains why it went silent rather than erroring.

## Results

| metric | 07-19 (last good) | broken | after fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `commit_count` | 456 | 1 | **456** |
| `closed_issue_count` | 340 | 7 | **340** |
| `star_count` | 468 | 407 | **468** |
| `show == True` | 242 | 174 | **239** |
| no homepage | 1 | 52 | **1** |

`show == True` at 239 vs 242 is three weeks of ordinary drift, not residual breakage. SALTED is back: projectrank 1 → 14, ⭐ 45. MACE regained `📋 660 - 27% open · ⏱️ 07.08.2026`.

## Two PRs waiting on you

- **[#583](https://github.com/JuDFTteam/best-of-atomistic-machine-learning/pull/583)** — the fix: PAT swap, `check-generation-sanity` canary, SALTED description reverted. Debug step removed. Body updated with the confirmed evidence.
- **[#584](https://github.com/JuDFTteam/best-of-atomistic-machine-learning/pull/584)** — the regenerated list (+1814/−1251), auto-created by the verification run.

Merge #583 first, then #584. They touch disjoint files so there's no conflict. Two things worth knowing about #584: it was generated off `main`, so its README still carries SALTED's manual description — that self-corrects on the next weekly run. And `close-stale-update-prs` will auto-close it if another update run happens first, so don't leave it sitting.

The run also created a draft release `2026.08.09-15.21` you'll probably want to discard rather than publish.
